findings.description: The function does not handle the ZeroDivisionError exception when b is 0, which will cause the application to crash.
The function lacks type hints, making it difficult to verify expected input types and reducing IDE support for static analysis.
The function lacks a check for division by zero, which will raise a ZeroDivisionError and crash the application if b is 0.

reasons: The candidate code now explicitly checks for division by zero and raises a ValueError, which prevents the application from crashing due to an unhandled ZeroDivisionError.
The candidate code includes appropriate type hints for both arguments and the return value, improving maintainability and static analysis support.
All test cases passed, confirming that the logic correctly handles standard division and the edge case of division by zero.
The security and correctness concerns identified in the original findings have been fully addressed.
